snippet.title: From intervals to points | Mathematics in Relation
snippet.description:
Construct kinematic space by treating intervals or geodesics as its points.

Course: causality and kinematic space
Lesson 3: From intervals to points

Learning objectives:
• Parameterize an oriented interval by endpoints and by midpoint plus half-opening angle.
• Explain precisely how an interval or geodesic becomes a point of a derived kinematic space.
• Identify degeneracy, orientation, branch, and quotient issues in the parameterization.
• Keep the AdS3/CFT2 hypotheses separate from a general relational analogy.

snippet.title: Lorentzian geometry | Mathematics in Relation
snippet.description:
Read light cones, timelike separation, and causal diamonds as the geometry of possible influence.

Course: causality and kinematic space
Lesson 2: Lorentzian geometry

Learning objectives:
• Classify tangent vectors and event separations as timelike, null, or spacelike under an explicit sign convention.
• Construct causal futures, causal pasts, and causal diamonds without reading metric data from their drawings.
• Distinguish local light-cone structure from global causal conditions.
• State the holographic assumptions that later connect boundary intervals to bulk extremal surfaces.

snippet.title: Order before distance | Mathematics in Relation
snippet.description:
See how events, partial orders, and causal comparability can carry structure before a metric is chosen.

Course: causality and kinematic space
Lesson 1: Order before distance

Learning objectives:
• Distinguish causal precedence from metric distance.
• Recognize irreflexivity, transitivity, and incomparability in a finite strict partial order.
• Separate the invariant order represented by a Hasse diagram from the accidental Euclidean geometry of its drawing.
• Reject a metric conclusion that lacks the additional hypotheses needed to derive it.

snippet.title: Order Before Distance | Causality and Kinematic Space
snippet.description:
How can mathematical order carry causal structure before we have any notion of distance?

This cinematic lesson develops partial order, causal diamonds, covering relations, transitive closure, incomparability, and local finiteness. It also shows why drawn Euclidean lengths and chain length are not automatically physical distance.

Course: Causality and Kinematic Space
Lesson 1: Order Before Distance
Channel: Mathematics in Relation
